info.title: Huddle Multi-Tenant E-Commerce API
info.description:
API for the Huddle multi-tenant e-commerce backend.

**Auth.** Tokens are JWTs that last 1 hour and carry a role. Admin routes need an **admin** token (from `/admin/signup` or `/admin/signin`). `/customer/profile` and `/customer/orders` need a **customer** token (from `/customer/signup` or `/customer/signin`). Using the wrong role returns 403.

**Responses.** Every response uses the same envelope: `{ success, message, data?, error? }`.

**Money.** Prices are returned as decimal strings, e.g. `"15000"` or `"1500.50"`. Requests accept a number or a string.

**Rate limit.** Sign-up and sign-in routes allow 60 requests per minute per IP, then return 429.

**Storefronts.** Storefront websites call `/storefront/*` and `/cart` with the store's key in the `X-Store-Key` header. The key is **publishable** (it is visible in storefront pages): it only identifies the store for public actions and never grants seller access.

**CORS.** Browser origins listed in `CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` (exact origins or wildcards like `https://*.huddle.ng`) may call the API with credentials; storefronts must send requests with `credentials: "include"` so the cart cookie is kept.

status.description: `needs_refund`: money arrived for an order that could no longer take it. `review`: the amount, currency or account did not match the order.

BadRequest.description: Invalid request body, query or values. For validation failures, `error` is a JSON object of field -> message, e.g. {"currency":"currency must be exactly 3 characters"}

Forbidden.description: Wrong token role, or the store/product belongs to another admin

Conflict.description: Already exists (names and emails are compared case-insensitively), or not enough stock

TooManyRequests.description: Rate limit exceeded (60 requests per minute per IP)

post.summary: Place an order from the cart
post.description:
Turns this store's cart (from the `cart_session` cookie) into a **pending** order. Prices are read from the products at this moment, stock is held for 30 minutes (`ORDER_HOLD_MINUTES`), and the cart is emptied. If the order is not paid in time it expires and the stock goes back on sale.

**Guests can check out.** If a customer token is sent, the order is linked to that account; a token that is invalid (401), not a customer token (403) or from another store (403) is refused, never ignored.

If any item is short of stock the whole order is refused and nothing is taken.

400.description: Validation failed, invalid phone, empty cart, or items in different currencies

403.description: Token is not a customer token of this store

409.description: An item is sold out, has too little stock (e.g. "Only 1 of Shoe left in stock") or is no longer available; or a checkout of this cart is already running

get.summary: View an order placed in this store
get.description: For the shopper's order page or receipt link. Orders of other stores return 404.
Newest first. Guest orders are not included.
Newest first, optionally filtered by status.

patch.description:
Allowed changes:
- `pending` → `paid` (the seller confirmed a transfer or cash payment)
- `pending` → `cancelled` (the held stock goes back on sale)
- `paid` → `fulfilled`

Anything else returns 409. `expired` is set only by the system.

409.description: Status change not allowed, e.g. "A cancelled order cannot be marked paid"

post.summary: Pay for an order with Bachs
post.description:
Opens a Bachs hosted checkout for a **pending** order and returns its `checkout_url`. The payment is charged to the store's Bachs sub-account, so the money lands in the seller's own balance. Calling again while that checkout is open returns the same one.

After paying, Bachs sends the shopper to `success_url` with `?checkout_id=...`. **That redirect is not proof of payment**: the order turns `paid` only when Bachs confirms it through the signed webhook, so the success page should poll `GET /storefront/orders/{id}` until the status is `paid`.

409.description: The order is already paid, no longer pending, about to expire, or the store can't take online payments yet

502.description: Bachs refused the payment (its reason is included) or could not be reached

503.description: Online payment is not set up on this server (BACHS_API_KEY)

post.description:
Called by Bachs, not by storefronts. Register this URL as two Bachs webhook endpoints, one for **Account events** and one for **Connected account events** (sellers' sub-accounts), since an endpoint listens to one source. Set `BACHS_WEBHOOK_SECRET` to both signing secrets, comma-separated.

Every delivery must carry a valid `X-Bachs-Signature-V2` (or `X-Bachs-Timestamp` + `X-Bachs-Signature`) made with one of the `BACHS_WEBHOOK_SECRET` secrets, no older than 5 minutes. Each event id is handled once.

Handled events: `checkout.completed` (with `payment_status: paid`) and `collection.succeeded` mark the order paid, after checking amount, currency and seller account; a mismatch is held for review. `checkout.expired` closes the checkout. `refund.created`, `refund.paid` and `refund.failed` settle refunds. `capability.updated` records whether a seller's account can take payments (see `GET /store/{id}/payments`). A payment for an order that expired is applied if the stock is still there, otherwise it is flagged for refund. Other events are acknowledged and ignored.

400.description: Bad signature or malformed event; Bachs will not retry

503.description: BACHS_WEBHOOK_SECRET is not set; Bachs retries

get.summary: Can the store take online payments?
get.description: Reads the store's Bachs account and returns whether shoppers can pay online (`ready`), the status of each capability and what Bachs still needs from the seller. Use it on the seller's return from onboarding: the return itself does not mean onboarding succeeded. If Bachs can't be reached, the last known statuses are returned.

post.summary: Set up online payments with Bachs
post.description:
Creates the store's Bachs account if it has none, then returns a single-use link to Bachs' hosted onboarding. Send the seller there straight away: each call replaces the previous link, and links expire.

Bachs sends the seller to `return_url` when they finish or leave; then check `GET /store/{id}/payments`. An expired or used link leads to `refresh_url`, which should call this endpoint again for a fresh link. Once the store is ready, the link lets the seller update their details instead.

The seller's money lands in this account's balance. In production a store can't take online payments until `ready` is true.

message.example: Open the link to set up payments

409.description: Nothing to update, or Bachs has suspended or rejected the account

502.description: Bachs refused the request (its reason is in the message) or could not be reached

503.description: Bachs is not configured on this server

get.summary: Payments that need the seller's attention
get.description: Payments with status `needs_refund` (money arrived for an order that expired and could no longer be filled, or that was already paid) or `review` (the amount, currency or account did not match). Refund them with `POST /store/{id}/payments/{paymentId}/refund`.

post.summary: Refund a payment, in full or in part
post.description:
Gives money back to the shopper from the seller's Bachs balance: the whole payment, or `amount` of it. Payments that are `paid`, `needs_refund` or `review` can be refunded. Bachs takes **one refund per payment**, so after a partial refund the rest can't be refunded later.

Bachs keeps its processing fee on a sale and does not give it back on a refund, so a seller whose balance is only that sale can't refund all of it. They get 409 with their available balance and can refund up to that.

The refund is usually `processing` at first; Bachs confirms it through the webhook. When it is `paid`, the payment becomes `refunded`. If this payment is what paid the order and the order is not fulfilled, the order is cancelled and its stock goes back on sale, unless `keep_order` is true (e.g. refunding one missing item while the rest is delivered).

If Bachs could not be reached (502), call again: the same refund is re-sent, never a second one. A `failed` refund can be tried again.

amount.description: Optional. Up to the payment's amount, at most 2 decimal places. Omit for a full refund.

400.description: Invalid amount (0 or less, more than the payment, more than 2 decimals) or reason too long

409.description: Already refunded, a refund is in progress, the payment can't be refunded in its status, Bachs has not confirmed its charge yet, or the seller's Bachs balance is too low (the message gives the available balance)

502.description: Bachs refused the refund (its reason is in the message) or could not be reached

503.description: Bachs is not configured on this server
